title: Chapter 3248 While You Were Gone
content:
Somehow, it worked.

Sunny had thought that there was only ash left in Neph’s heart, but he still managed to bring a feeble flame of aspiration back to life. She agreed to meet Cassie and undergo the same journey Sunny had gone on — the journey of experiencing her original life anew.

He was not sure what it was exactly that had convinced her. Maybe it was his appeal to her conviction; perhaps it was his reminder of what her true goal was.

Maybe she had come ready to be convinced, to begin with.

Still, he wanted to believe that it was the memories of their life together. Of the bond they shared and the love they had enjoyed... of the promises they had given.

He wanted to learn more, to talk to her more — but, at that point, the Jade Queen finally decided to get involved. Stepping easily off the parapet, she appeared near Sunny and Nephis in the blink of an eye.

It seemed that she could barely wait to meet her idol, as well as welcome the First Ruler as a queen.

So, before Sunny could insert a word, Nephis was whisked away. He stared at her back longingly, a thousand unsaid words boiling in his heart, but there was little he could do... at least if he wanted to act wisely.

There was no point in rushing, anyway. They had plenty of time.

‘Slow and steady wins the race.'

As the gates of the Jade Palace opened and countless attendants poured out to welcome White Abyss with the pomp and honor she deserved, he signed and finally looked away.

It was only then Sunny realized that he had been left alone with Sable.

Well... and Slayer.

Ignoring Sable's gaze, which was boring holes into his face, he turned to the malevolent Shadow and lingered for a moment.

Eventually, he spoke:

“You did well... thank you, Orphne."

In truth, back in his days as Shadow, he had completely forgotten Slayer's existence, leaving her to wander the terrifying reaches of the Nightmare alone for countless years. The task he had given her — keep Sable alive — must not have been an easy one, either. But she had performed her duty well.

Remembering the uneasy beginning of their relationship, when he had to defeat her in a duel and feed her his blood every time he needed something from her, Sunny could not help but ponder how far they had come.

Time was truly a wondrous thing.

In response to his praise, Slayer remained motionless for a long while, then nodded curtly.

A moment later, she dissolved into a torrent of darkness, returning into the nourishing black flames of his soul... without waiting for his command or asking permission to do so, either.

Sunny suddenly felt terrible.

Here he was, lecturing Nephis about how irresponsible it was to abandon shadows, while he had basically thrown Slayer out and left her homeless for centuries.

‘Still!’

Clearing his throat, he looked at Sable.

‘Did she have to leave me alone with Smile of Heaven?’

Caught in the moment, Sunny had said everything he needed to say in order to convince Nephis. Now, though, he became painfully aware of the fact that he had said all those things in front of her mother.

Who was younger than her daughter by a few thousand years.

Sadly, that did not make the situation any less awkward.

Sunny sighed.

‘That's also progress, though, is it not?'

He had not known that he was still able to feel awkwardness.

Shifting restlessly under Sable's burning gaze, Sunny forced out a smile.

“We should probably enter the palace, too."

She stared for a few moments, then returned his smile.

“That sounds like a great idea! After all..."

Her voice lowered.

"We have a lot of catching up to do..."

At the end there, it sounded a little ominous.

Sunny laughed nervously.

‘I don't suppose Mordret will decide to get involved in this conversation, either? Damn it... damn bastard! He's no help at all!'

***

"You said a lot of strange things back there, Sunny."

“Ah... yes, ma'am.”

"Ma'am? What's with the polite tone? Hey, I am still a young lady! Aren't you thousands of years old?"

“Ah, ha-ha... yeah, you're right. Sable."

“Huh? Aren't you speaking a little too comfortably now?"

“Am I? Oh, I guess I am. S—sorry."

Sable gave him a long, incredulous look. They were currently in a windowless room that looked like a wine cellar. The Jade Queen and Nephis were having an audience at the moment, so Sunny and Sable had simply gone to find a quiet corner to talk. She led him here with confident steps, looked around, then picked out a bottle and procured two glasses out of somewhere, as well as some light snacks.

"Uh... this is the Jade Queen's cellar. Perhaps we shouldn't just drink from a random bottle."

Sable just gave him a dubious look.

“I've been to this cellar a hundred times. I know which bottles are poisoned, which ones will turn you into a Nightmare Creature, which ones will get a Master drunk in one sip, and which ones are safe to drink."

‘Oh. Right.’

In the future, the Jade Palace would belong to Ki Song. As members of the same cohort, Sable and Ki Song would have been quite close — close enough for Sable to know the Jade Palace like the back of her hand, at least, even if traveling between Citadels had been far more difficult back then.

She opened the bottle, poured both of them a glass of glistening golden liquid, and then sat down on a stray crate. Sunny sighed and sat, as well.

‘I wonder... does she know that it was her daughter who killed Ki Song, in the end?’

Sable shifted awkwardly, trying to fold her wings in a comfortable way, then gave them a long look.

“These things are useful, but carrying them around all day is a hassle. I really miss my human body sometimes."

For a moment, her gaze turned distant.

“I wonder what happened to it, all those years ago. It was probably swallowed by an abomination or was left to rot on the ruins of America, right?"

Then, she flinched.

“No, that can't be right. If Nephis was born, then it means that my body had been recovered."

Sunny lingered for a moment, then nodded.

“Actually, it's in the Ivory Tower."

Noticing a confused expression on Sable's face, he explained.

“The Tower of Hope — in the future, it's Neph's Citadel. She has been taking care of your body for a long while... ever since her grandmother passed away, shortly before her First Nightmare. Ah, but she was away for a few years — during that time, you were kept in a special care facility. I even brought you flowers, once or twice."

He remained silent for a few moments.

“Everyone assumed that you were Hollow. Well... I guess your body was, in a sense."

Sable studied him silently, then asked:

“What is the world like? What was it like before you entered this Nightmare, at least?"

Sunny smiled joylessly and looked away.

“Are you sure you want to know?"

She nodded.

“Yes, I do. Nephis... has not been very talkative on the way here. And she dragged Sister Orphne and me across the mortal realms in a matter of days — people must think that there's a stray comet piercing one sky after another. There has not been a lot of time to talk."

Sunny remained silent for a short while, then sighed.

“Well, the world is dying. I am not sure how much you know — humanity's reservoir of knowledge was much shallower three decades ago, after all — but our world is being consumed by the Dream Realm, bit by bit."

He considered how history must have looked from Sable's perspective, then shook his head dejectedly.

“You don't know, do you? Humanity was on a slow, but constant rise for as long as you were alive. But things changed after that Gate opened in America. After you died... went missing. One would think that losing an entire continent would have graver repercussions than the death of one Master, but it was actually the other way around. Anyway, America was a breaking point — after that, it has been a constant descent for us."

Sunny shrugged.

“We lost America. Broken Sword went missing a few years later. The Immortal Flame clan fell into obscurity. By the time Nephis and I were in our twenties, we lost Antarctica, as well. Humanity was on the brink... and what did humans do in that precarious situation? That's right, our two Supremes decided to embroil all of humanity in a bloody civil war. The House of Night was all but wiped out, countless Awakened perished. Naturally, there were losses among the civilian population as a result."

Looking at Sable's pale face, he sighed.

“That was when Nephis and I staged a little revolt and killed both Sovereigns, attaining Supremacy ourselves in the process. I hid in the shadows, while she stepped into the light to wear the crown of humanity. We've been trying to keep the world from being entirely destroyed since then... but it has been hard. The process is irreversible. All we can do is help humanity leave our dying homeworld and settle safely in the Dream Realm."

His expression darkened.

“The problem is that we are already barely hanging in there. And once our world is entirely consumed, there will be a chain reaction causing the fallen deities of the Dream Realm to rise from their slumber... the Cursed abominations, as well as those who are Unholy. I know that my power seems impossible to you, but I have faced Unholy Nightmare Creatures twice. And each time, I barely escaped, surviving by the skin of my teeth. I felt like an ant facing a giant."

Sunny looked at Sable somberly and added:

“The only way to ensure that humanity is not devoured by those fallen gods is to become gods ourselves. It is a race against time... that is why we entered the Fifth Nightmare. Me, Nephis, Cassie, and Mordret."

Sable's eyebrows rose.

“Mordret? Anvil's boy?"

Sunny smiled darkly and looked away.

“Yeah. Something like that."

She remained silent for a long while, then turned away with a mournful expression.

"I guess it's true, then. That everyone is dead. There is no way my peers or my elders would have allowed you children to challenge the Nightmare alone if they were still alive.”

Sunny's tried to smile.

“Children? Didn't you mention that I was a few thousand years old?"

Sable looked down, then nodded silently.

Then, she looked at him with a stern frown.

“So, the world is ending. I get it. But more importantly — what, exactly, is going on between you and my daughter? Huh?"

Sunny, who had been taking a sip of the golden liquid, coughed and spat it out.

His face turned a shade paler.

"Well... that, uh... you see... her Aspect Legacy! Her Aspect Legacy, that's the thing... her Aspect Legacy has a branch called the Knowledge of Passion, and so..."

The more he talked, the sterner Sable's expression seemed to become.

And the more cold sweat rolled down Sunny's back.

‘How, how did I end up in this situation?!’

Was it the damn [Fated] Attribute?!

Maybe he should have stayed in the Shadow Realm, after all.
